correctness.rationale: For every n, f(n)=sum over exact prime powers of p^{-a}; finite CRT cylinders converge to independent p-adic geometric variables, and their omitted mean is uniformly bounded by sum_{p>P}1/p^2. The Erdős–Wintner criterion establishes continuity because sum_p1/p diverges. For y->infinity the no-p<=y event supplies M(y)(1-O(1/log y)) below F(1/y), since the independent tail expectation is O(1/(y log y)). The necessary local condition X_p<=1/y gives upper product M(y)exp(O(y^{-1/2})). Mertens gives e^{-gamma}/log y. The Pareto ratio is F(t^alpha)/F(t), with alpha>=1. The exact checker covers only finite arithmetic identities; no inference from numerical truncation is used.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 w_1 paper proves positive value-set density, while the classical Erdős–Wintner theorem gives existence/continuity and Mertens evaluates a prime-avoidance product. None of the inspected theorem statements asserts the exact normalized reciprocal-prime-power endpoint equivalence; actual published-index and literature searches found no covering w(n)/n law. An unindexed/general small-deviation theorem remains a live residual risk.
residual_risks: No search establishes novelty. A generic published but unindexed small-ball theorem for bounded nonnegative additive prime weights might imply this endpoint as a special case.

value.rationale: The exact natural-density lower-endpoint behavior of the normalized w_1 function is a motivated distributional invariant of the current Erdős function, contrasting with its unnormalized image cardinality. It identifies the sharp Mertens coefficient and a complete Pareto-scale conditional profile over every fixed exponent alpha>=1. This is an infinite family of distribution statements, not a single small finite case or mere sample verification; the proof excludes unclaimed joint-threshold and upper-tail conclusions.
